skill.name: incident-responder
skill.description: Guides SRE incident response with severity assessment, incident command, observability-driven investigation, recovery validation, stakeholder communication, and blameless post-incident reviews.
skill.summary: Structured SRE guidance for production incidents, recovery, communication, and post-incident learning.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Production incidents need fast triage, clear roles, and accurate communication. This skill gives SRE teams structured response steps, recovery checks, and post-incident improvement guidance.
actual_capabilities: Classifies incident severity and business impact.
Defines incident command roles and communication cadence.
Guides observability-based investigation using metrics, logs, and traces.
Plans recovery with rollback, validation, and monitoring steps.
Structures stakeholder updates for internal and external audiences.
Supports blameless post-incident reviews and action tracking.
limitations: It does not connect to monitoring tools, ticketing systems, or incident platforms.
It relies on user-provided metrics, logs, timelines, and service context.
It cannot replace incident commander authority, regulatory counsel, or internal escalation policies.
The referenced implementation playbook is not included in the scanned package.

use_cases.title: Triage a Production Outage
use_cases.description: Triage an outage, classify severity, identify likely causes, and choose the safest first actions.

use_cases.title: Coordinate a Live Incident
use_cases.description: Set roles, coordinate updates, track decisions, and keep stakeholders aligned during a live incident.

use_cases.title: Improve Reliability After Recovery
use_cases.description: Turn incident data into blameless reviews, action items, and reliability improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Classify an Incident
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me classify this incident. Service: [service]. Symptoms: [symptoms]. User impact: [impact]. Recent changes: [changes]. Current metrics: [metrics].

prompt_templates.title: Create a Response Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a response plan for a P1 incident affecting [service]. Include roles, first actions, communication cadence, validation checks, and escalation points.

prompt_templates.title: Guide a Live Investigation
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide a live investigation for [service]. Use these signals: [metrics], [logs], [traces], [deployments], and [dependencies]. Prioritize reversible actions.

prompt_templates.title: Build Post-Incident Improvements
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a post-incident review for [incident]. Include timeline, impact, contributing factors, follow-up actions, owners, due dates, and SLO lessons.

output_examples.input: A checkout service has a 12 percent error rate after a deployment.
output_examples.output: Likely severity is P1 if purchases are blocked for many users. Roll back or disable the risky change, assign incident roles, and validate checkout success.

output_examples.input: Create first actions for a latency spike across three regions.
output: Declare an incident commander and communication lead.
Freeze risky deployments until rollback safety is clear.
Compare error rate, latency, and saturation across the last deployment window.
Post customer-facing updates every 30 minutes until service stabilizes.

output_examples.input: Summarize what a post-incident review should capture.
output: Document the timeline, customer impact, and decisions made during response.
Identify contributing system factors without assigning blame.
Create owned action items for prevention, detection, and response improvements.

best_practices: Start with user impact, severity, and rollback safety before deep root cause analysis.
Keep a dated timeline of actions, decisions, owners, and observed system changes.
Validate recovery with SLIs, customer experience signals, and dependency health checks.
anti_patterns: Do not run broad changes before confirming rollback paths and blast radius.
Do not delay stakeholder updates until root cause is fully known.
Do not treat the postmortem as a blame exercise or ticket list.

faq.question: Can this skill manage a live production incident?
faq.answer: It can guide triage, roles, communication, investigation, recovery, and documentation. A human incident commander still owns decisions.

faq.question: Does it connect to PagerDuty, Datadog, or Slack?
faq.answer: No. It provides response guidance and checklists, but it does not integrate with external tools.

faq.question: What information should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide affected services, user impact, recent changes, key metrics, logs, traces, and current mitigation steps.

faq.question: Can it help write customer updates?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft status updates with impact, mitigation progress, next update time, and recovery confirmation.

faq.question: Is it only for SRE teams?
faq.answer: No. It is useful for platform teams, application teams, support leads, and engineering managers during incidents.

faq.question: Can it perform root cause analysis?
faq.answer: It can structure analysis after recovery. It needs accurate timelines, system context, and evidence from the response.
